cards.title: PBPK Platform Qualification and Regulatory Impact
cards.claim: PBPK platforms must be qualified for their intended use before being used to support regulatory decisions. The extent of qualification required depends on the regulatory impact of the modelling (low, moderate, or high). High-impact analyses (e.g., replacing clinical data, predicting DDIs in specific populations) require rigorous demonstration of the platform's ability to predict observed outcomes using pre-specified qualification datasets. Low-impact analyses (e.g., mechanistic understanding where confirmatory PK data exists) may not require formal platform qualification.
conditions: Applicable when PBPK modelling is intended to support a regulatory decision.
Qualification is purpose-specific and platform-version specific.
For high-impact analyses, the science must be mature enough, supported by valid system data and in vitro-in vivo correlations.
required_inputs: Definition of the intended regulatory purpose.
For high impact: Pre-specified qualification datasets with in vivo data for probe drugs.
Documentation of system-dependent parameters and their justification.
limitations: Qualification issued within a specific submission is valid only for that submission unless a CHMP qualification opinion exists.
Abstract-only material supports only what appears in the abstract; this guideline is full-text but excerpts are partial.
Does not define specific numerical acceptance criteria for 'adequacy' of prediction; this is case-by-case.
cards.downstream_use: Guides the selection of validation datasets and the level of documentation required for human simulation scenarios. Determines whether a generic PBPK platform can be used or if specific drug-model validation is mandatory.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
